name: Kumm Curry
subtitle: quick hill mushroom curry heavy with black pepper and coconut

ingredients.note: wild mushrooms after the first rains are the Kodagu version; button or oyster mushrooms stand in well
the defining flavour, crush it fresh

prepNotes: Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of washing them; soaked mushrooms release water into the pan and refuse to brown.
Slice them thick, about 1 cm. Thin slices disappear into the gravy.
Crush the black pepper coarsely just before cooking.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and fry the onion over medium heat until soft and gold, about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes until fragrant.
Turn the heat high, add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 minutes so they colour on one side.
steps.tip: A crowded pan steams instead of browning. Use the widest pan you have, or cook in two batches.

steps.text: Stir and cook 4 minutes more, until the water the mushrooms release has boiled away.
Lower the heat, add the turmeric, coriander powder and half the crushed pepper and fry 1 minute.
Add the grated coconut and fry 2 minutes, until it smells toasted and looks dry.
Pour in the water with 3/4 tsp salt, cover and simmer 6 minutes.
Uncover, stir in the rest of the pepper and cook 3 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat the mushrooms.
steps.tip: Adding half the pepper at the end keeps its sharpness; pepper cooked from the start goes flat and woody.

steps.text: Check the salt, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve with rice or otti.

storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat quickly over high heat so the mushrooms do not go rubbery.
